correctness.rationale: The exact angle parametrization gives \(Q(\gamma,u)=(y-z)/(c-b)\) on the full domain \(0<\gamma<u<1\). The denominator is positive. The sign numerator of \(\partial_u\log Q\) has derivative \(-2u-4\gamma^3-6\gamma^2<0\), so no interior minimum exists. Endpoint limits are \(1\) and \(f(2\gamma)\); the derivative of \(f\) has the unique cubic zero \(q\), yielding the exact sharp constant. Sharpness follows by \(2\cos p=q\) and \(\delta\downarrow0\).

value.rationale: This closes an explicit 2008 sharp-constant conjecture for a classical Euclidean geometry theorem. The result replaces finite integer-side evidence by an exact proof, identifies the best global robustness constant, and locates the unique limiting similarity class forcing sharpness. It is not a routine restatement of Steiner–Lehmus.
